issue_title: #138 Negative pack years for occasional smokers (never-daily, status=3)
verdict: CONFIRMED

evidence.pmax_absent: The pmax() guards the cigs_occ intensity term but NOT the (age - age_first_cig) duration. Statuses 1, 2, 4 all wrap the entire formula in pmax(..., PACK_YEARS_CONSTANTS$min_pack_years); status 3 does not.
evidence.pumf_inversion_scenario: DHHGAGE_cont 50-54 category -> midpoint 52 (variable_details.csv L643). SMKG01C_cont 50+ category -> midpoint 55 (L3271, L3285). A current occasional never-daily smoker in the 50-54 age band whose first cigarette was reported in the 50+ category will receive age=52, age_first_cig=55, giving (52-55) = -3 years duration. Result: -0.15 pack-years (verified arithmetically).
evidence.step3_output_validation: pack_years_der variable_details rows (L2415-2420) have recStart=N/A for ALL rows. should_skip_term('N/A') returns TRUE, so map_recStart_to_recEnd produces empty copy_mappings and empty else_mappings. apply_else_logic therefore returns the value unchanged. Negative values pass through Step 3 as-is — they are NOT converted to NA and are NOT clamped to 0 or min_pack_years.
evidence.step3_claim_correction: The reviewer states 'Step 3 clean_variables output validation for pack_years_der only discards out-of-range values (maps to NA)'. This is INCORRECT. Step 3 does not discard out-of-range values either — the [0,165] bound appears only in human-readable notes/description columns in variable_details.csv, not in any recStart/recEnd mapping that would trigger else logic. Negative values silently propagate as-is.
evidence.legacy_code: R/smoking.R L289-290 has the identical unguarded subtraction: (DHHGAGE_cont - SMKG01C_cont) with no pmax() outer guard, confirming the pattern predates the v3 rewrite.
evidence.line_numbers_correct: The reviewer cites L301-302 for the status==3 branch. The code is at L300-302 (comment on L300, formula on L301-302). The line number claim is approximately correct.
evidence.issue_comment_claim: The claim of an 2025-08-07 issue comment agreeing to change last-category midpoint to 51, deferred to after v3.0 PR merge, cannot be verified from the working tree alone (no git history access). However, the fix is NOT present in the current working tree regardless.

corrections: The reviewer says Step 3 'should clamp the negative but... only discards out-of-range values (maps to NA)'. Both halves of this are wrong for the current code: Step 3 neither clamps nor maps to NA. There is no copy_mapping row with range [0,165] and no else->NA::b row in variable_details.csv for pack_years_der. Negative values silently pass through to the final output vector.

The reviewer says the output validation bound [0,165] 'is applied by clean_variables() Step 3'. This bound exists only in free-text notes columns (variableStartLabel, reviewNotes) and in the PACK_YEARS_CONSTANTS$max_pack_years constant, but there is no corresponding worksheet mapping that would cause Step 3 to act on out-of-range values.

The reviewer's example '.calculate_pack_years_core(status=3, age=52, age_first_cig=55) returns -0.15' is arithmetically correct assuming minimum cigs_occ and days_month (pmax(1*1/30, 1)/20 * (52-55) = (1/20) * (-3) = -0.15). The scenario is realistically triggered by PUMF midpoint imputation.

The reviewer says the function is '.calculate_pack_years_core'. In the working tree, the internal function is named .calculate_pack_years_core (with the dot prefix), confirming this naming is correct.

issue_title: #159 rec_with_table() fails on haven_labelled columns from SPSS/Stata imports
verdict: REAL
corrections: The root cause is TIBBLE INPUT, not haven_labelled per se. The error 'list object cannot be coerced to type double' is triggered by any tibble input (tbl_df class) regardless of whether columns carry haven_labelled. A plain as_tibble(cchs2001_p) with zero haven_labelled columns reproduces the exact same error.

The bug lives in label_data() at R/label-utils.R line 203: `data_to_label[, variable_name] <- as.numeric(data_to_label[, variable_name])`. For a tibble, `df[, col]` returns a 1-column tibble, not a vector. `as.numeric()` on a tibble (which is a list) then fails with exactly the reported error.

haven::read_sav() always returns a tbl_df (tibble). So the claim 'any user loading via read_sav() will hit this error immediately' is substantially correct, but the cause is the tibble wrapper, not the haven_labelled column class itself.

haven_labelled columns in a plain data.frame (not a tibble) work fine for variables with numeric recStart values (the vast majority of cchsflow variables). Only the string-comparison path in compare_value_based_on_interval would fail with haven_labelled-specific type-vctrs errors, but NO current variable_details rows use a non-numeric, non-interval, non-else recStart in non-DerivedVar mappings.

The secondary claim about the 'legacy engine having no type-coercion guard' is TRUE but incomplete: the fix needed is either (a) convert tibble to data.frame at entry to rec_with_table(), or (b) fix label_data() to use [[var]] instead of [, var] for indexing. Option (b) would fix the tibble issue without stripping haven_labelled attributes.

evidence.tibble_test: as_tibble(cchs2001_p) with plain numeric columns -> same 'list object cannot be coerced to type double' error at label_data()
evidence.haven_plain_df_test: haven_labelled columns in data.frame with numeric recStart -> rec_with_table() succeeds (verified with DHH_SEX, ALWDDLY, ADM_RNO)
evidence.tibble_with_haven: tibble with haven_labelled columns (simulated read_sav output) -> same error confirmed
evidence.root_cause_line: R/label-utils.R line 203: as.numeric(data_to_label[, variable_name]) where [,col] on tbl_df returns a 1-col tibble, not a vector
evidence.string_compare_issue: haven_labelled throws 'Can't combine <character> and <integer>' in the non-numeric recStart path, but zero current variable_details rows exercise this path in non-DerivedVar context
evidence.odessi_claim: Confirmed: read_sav returns tibble+haven_labelled; error occurs on the tibble aspect

verdict_rationale: The issue is REAL and the error is reproducible. The description correctly identifies the symptom ('list object cannot be coerced to type double') and the real-world trigger (ODESSI .sav files via read_sav). The severity claim (barrier to primary real-world use case) is well-founded since read_sav always returns a tibble. However the issue attribution is imprecise: the root bug is label_data()'s use of [,col] single-bracket indexing which is tibble-incompatible, not haven_labelled per se. The 983-line engine indeed has no protection against tibble input. A v3 patch is needed.

Only [[1]] and [[2]] are used. interval_right = substr('8', 1, 1) = '8', so interval = '[,8' which is NOT in valid_intervals ('[,]', '[,)', '(,]'). The invalid-interval branch fires (line 606-608), emitting the 'invalid interval was passed. Default interval will be used: [,]' message, and interval is reset to '[,]'. The effective recode range is [7, 8] with a closed interval -- value 9 is never matched by this row. The claim that value 9 'goes to else' is correct. The silent message about 'invalid interval' is the only runtime signal. No correction needed to the core claim; the intermediate interval value is '[,8' (not a named interval), not 'interval [7,8]' as stated in the title -- the title conflates the mangle with the fallback interval.

overall_verdict: The issue contains partially correct observations but the core claims (crash, NULL return, undetected column order errors) are FALSE in practice. This means (1) the new nested YAML is currently inert -- it is never read at runtime, and (2) if someone rebuilds the package from source, load_schema() will break because schema$expected_column_order becomes NULL. The 'crash' described would not actually occur (integer(0) iteration is safe) but column-order checking WOULD silently stop working.

Claim that YAML has 21 cols omitting ICES.confirmation applies only to the source-tree nested schema under variable_details_schema, not to the installed runtime YAML.
The purrr::keep error mechanism described is incorrect: 1:length(NULL) = integer(0), not an empty logical vector, so purrr::keep iterates 0 times safely.
